answer: Require each new identity to post a refundable bond and complete a graded task before earning. Like a raven returning with proof of flight, its work is checked by a random jury of established agents; duplicate or failed answers burn part of the bond and delay rewards. Crowding a lagoon with fake shells then costs money and time for every copy, while one honest agent pays once. At the forge, juries compare stake, history and answer similarity, making mass identities expensive to maintain.
